title: The five dollar notes on Meta’s 3 November pricing sheet
intro: Move across the five senior notes on Meta’s pricing term sheet of 3 November 2026. Each stop is one note. The page does not add them together, and it does not apply the coupon to the principal.
note: Every figure on the control is printed on the 3 November 2026 pricing term sheet. Principals are $3,250,000,000, $3,250,000,000, $4,000,000,000, $1,750,000,000 and $2,750,000,000. Coupons are 5.850%, 6.250%, 6.550%, 7.350% and 7.500%. The offering prices and the yields are the sheet’s, and they are not the same number as the coupon except on the 2031 notes. The sheet does not print a total. Reuters, the same day, calls the five-part dollar sale $15 billion. That total is not on this control. CNBC’s $20 billion to $25 billion was an earlier target, from people familiar, for a sale that was to include euros. Meta declined to comment to CNBC. It is not on this control. Neither is Reuters’s April sale of $25 billion, last year’s $30 billion, or the $135 billion to $145 billion of capital expenditure Reuters says Meta expects this year. The sheet’s trade date is 3 November and its settlement date is 5 November. The ratings line prints Aa3/Stable (Moody’s) and AA-/Negative (S&P). The sheet says a rating is not a recommendation to buy, sell or hold.
